## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The old word commentary (*padabhājanīya*) to this rule defines the content of the instruction as instruction given by means of the eight *garudhamma*s or another teaching [Hüsken 1997].
The rule is widely preserved across monastic lineages. Full parallels cataloged by SuttaCentral include the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra*, as well as the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅgas and Pātimokkhas of the Dharmaguptaka (Pc 141), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 100), Sarvāstivāda (Pc 151), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese Pc 127; Tibetan Pc 167), Mahāsāṃghika (Pc 132), and Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravāda (Pc 132) traditions [SuttaCentral; Kieffer-Pülz 1997]. In addition, DharmaNexus records 198 internal text-reuse matches across 65 Pali texts, predominantly consisting of shared shared procedural phrasing with other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules (such as Pc 57, Pc 58, Pc 54, and Pc 95), along with cross-language alignments to Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* fragments [DharmaNexus].
